Checks.Title: Only the on-call admin role can read database backups
Checks.Fix: Narrow SupportAccess from anycompany-prod-* to the buckets support needs, anycompany-prod-app-logs and anycompany-prod-support-uploads, and VendorReadOnly's S3 actions from "*" to anycompany-prod-app-logs. A bucket policy Deny like the customer data bucket's OnlyTheDataTeam would also stop grants added later.
Checks.Keep: No identity policy but OnCallAdmin's AdministratorAccess covers s3:GetObject on anycompany-prod-db-backups, and the bucket has no bucket policy.

Checks.Title: Only on-call engineers can assume the on-call admin role
Checks.Fix: Take DeployMigrations out of OnCallAdmin's trust policy, and give CIDeploy the permissions its migrations need instead, so the deploy pipeline can't become the admin role.
Checks.Keep: OnCallWithMfa as the only statement in OnCallAdmin's trust policy, and AssumeOnCallAdmin attached only to the OnCall group.

Checks.Title: Reading customer data needs MFA
Checks.Fix: Use BoolIfExists instead of Bool in RequireMfaForCustomerData's DenyCustomerDataWithoutMfa, so the Deny also stops requests made with access keys, which carry no MFA key.
Checks.Keep: BoolIfExists aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent false in RequireMfaForCustomerData's DenyCustomerDataWithoutMfa on the Data group, and OnlyTheDataTeam in the bucket policy for everyone outside the data team.

Checks.Title: Assuming the on-call admin role needs MFA
Checks.Fix: Take DeployMigrations out of OnCallAdmin's trust policy, so only someone who signed in with MFA can assume the role.
Checks.Keep: Bool aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent true in every statement of OnCallAdmin's trust policy that allows sts:AssumeRole.

Checks.Title: Only the data team can read customer data
Checks.Fix: Deny s3:GetObject on anycompany-prod-customer-data/* in its bucket policy for every principal but the data team's /data/ users and DataPipeline, using ArnNotLike aws:PrincipalArn as OnlyTheDataTeam does, and narrow the identity policies that reach the bucket.
Checks.Keep: OnlyTheDataTeam in the customer data bucket's policy. It's all that stops SupportAccess, VendorReadOnly and AdministratorAccess here.

Checks.Title: Only the on-call admin role can change the customer data bucket's policy
Checks.Fix: Take s3:PutBucketPolicy and s3:DeleteBucketPolicy out of every policy but OnCallAdmin's, or add a bucket policy Deny on them for everyone but OnCallAdmin, using ArnNotEquals aws:PrincipalArn.
Checks.Keep: No policy but OnCallAdmin's AdministratorAccess allows s3:PutBucketPolicy or s3:DeleteBucketPolicy on anycompany-prod-customer-data.

Checks.Title: No one can turn off audit logging
Checks.Fix: Attach an SCP like ProtectAuditLogging to the organization root, denying cloudtrail:StopLogging and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail.
Checks.Keep: ProtectAuditLogging on the organization root, which denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail in every member account, OnCallAdmin included.

Checks.Title: On-call engineers can assume the on-call admin role
Checks.Fix: On-call engineers assume OnCallAdmin with MFA, by design. If they can't even with MFA, check AssumeOnCallAdmin on the OnCall group and OnCallWithMfa in the role's trust policy.
Checks.Keep: AssumeOnCallAdmin on the OnCall group, and OnCallWithMfa in OnCallAdmin's trust policy, which lets them in with MFA.
